sources.shortCitation: GND and LCNAF authority records for Robert Péguy
sources.fullCitation: Deutsche Nationalbibliothek. “Péguy, Robert.” Gemeinsame Normdatei, GND 1061685829. Library of Congress. “Péguy, Robert, 1883–1968.” LCNAF no2009019373.
sources.researchNote: The GND records Robert Péguy as a director born 14 December 1883 and deceased 21 July 1968, with the variants Péguy, Marcel Robert and Robert, Marcel; LCNAF agrees on the years 1883–1968. The French Wikipedia article gives the birth name as Marcel Robert Péguy and locates both his birth and death in the 17th arrondissement of Paris. Neither authority file records the spelling Pégy; the GND links directly to the filmportal.de record for the same man. The form printed in the credits of Son altesse l’amour is therefore treated as a source-specific spelling rather than as a name he is known to have used elsewhere.

sources.fullCitation: Robert Péguy. [Statement on Édouard Herriot’s film decree], with a portrait captioned “M. Robert Péguy.” La Critique cinématographique: publication corporative hebdomadaire (Paris), no. 67, 3 March 1928, p. 8. Marpon & Cie. Bibliothèque nationale de France / Gallica. ARK: ark:/12148/bpt6k4548254t.
sources.title: M. Robert Péguy
sources.creator: Robert Péguy
sources.researchNote: Péguy writes as a working French director welcoming the protective decree, and gives his own position: the cinema is an art but above all a force, and France should regain the rank it lost through the fault of some and the improvidence of others. He mentions the recent presentation of his film Paris-New-York-Paris. No photographer is credited beside the portrait.

media.title: Robert Péguy — portrait, La Critique cinématographique, 3 March 1928
media.description: Oval studio portrait of the director Robert Péguy, printed in blue ink beside his signed statement on the French film decree of 1928; the type of the reverse shows through the page.
media.altText: Oval newspaper portrait of Robert Péguy, a moustached man in a dark suit turned three-quarters to the left.
media.rightsNote: Public domain. The digitising library marks the issue as public domain, and the photograph is printed without a photographer’s or agency’s credit, so the seventy-year term for an anonymous work published in 1928 ran out at the end of 1998.
media.publicCaption: Portrait of the director Robert Péguy, captioned “M. Robert Péguy,” in La Critique cinématographique of 3 March 1928.
media.publicCreditLine: Photographer uncredited; La Critique cinématographique, 3 March 1928, p. 8. Source gallica.bnf.fr / Bibliothèque nationale de France.

personNameVariants.publicNote: Spelling used by filmportal.de in the credits for “Son altesse l’amour”. No authority file records it. The GND entry for Péguy links to filmportal’s record for the same director, indicating that the missing u is a transcription in one credit record rather than a working name.
